minutes.headline: Sewer Commission accepted its FY2024 annual report, pending corrected numbers, before Friday's deadline; billing errors and demand letters discussed.
minutes.summary: The vice chair, standing in for the chair, ran a short meeting. The commission voted by roll call to accept the FY2024 annual report on the condition that highlighted figures are finalized and initialed. Staff reported on a quarterly billing upload that doubled some bills, the still-broken demand letters in MUNIS, the search for an assistant business manager, and a delayed manhole repair.

attendees.role: vice chair, standing in for Mike Mackin

votes.motion: Accept the FY2024 annual report with the caveat that the yellow-highlighted numbers are finalized and changes initialed before the Friday submission deadline.

budget_items.what_was_said: Some figures highlighted in yellow in the report are from past years and need updating by staff before submission.
A member asked how the proposed rate increase was calculated; the answer was that it reflected increased contract rates at the facility where sewage is sent for treatment.
A file upload into MUNIS doubled some bills in the latest quarterly billing, and affected customers who called in had their bills corrected.
MUNIS still cannot send demand letters on late accounts, a problem over a year old; the letters would carry a late fee and interest.

decisions.decision: The vice chair will ask the director to contact the member who intends to resign to prompt a formal resignation letter so a replacement can be sought.
Next agenda to include billing update, the assistant business manager position, and the manhole repair.
Hiring for the assistant business manager waits on a second interview the next morning, then reference checks by HR, before any decision.
A pre-construction meeting will be set up for the manhole repair once the frost leaves.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call to accept its FY2024 annual report, on condition that highlighted figures are finalized and initialed before Friday's deadline.
Some figures highlighted in the report come from past years, and staff must update them before the report is submitted.
A file upload into MUNIS doubled some bills in the latest quarterly billing; customers who called in had their bills corrected.
MUNIS still cannot send demand letters on late accounts, a problem more than a year old.
Hiring for the assistant business manager waits on a second interview and HR reference checks, and a manhole repair meeting waits for the frost to leave.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills come from this commission's billing system, and a doubled bill or a late account that gets no demand letter is a billing problem that lands on ratepayers or on collections.
The annual report was accepted before its numbers were final, so what the town files depends on staff corrections that the minutes show only as a condition, not as a completed check.
